pages.title: NPC memory and identity
pages.subtitle: Qwen3.5-9B is selected after testing. All four local models remain available.

images.caption: Actual camp: Nusa recalls the secret word, distinguishes the player’s claim from their shared family records, and answers age 20.

blocks.text: Spoken dialogue now uses proper user/assistant history. Important things a person says are saved separately and attributed to them; private intentions no longer crowd out speech. Recall questions are excluded from durable statements. NPC requests include separate identities, ages, family relationships and rendered hair colours.

When the player claimed two children, Nusa replied: “That is not true. We only have one child, Taho.” Asked later what the player said, Nusa correctly recalled two. The game’s family records remained unchanged.

Use the existing shortcut. Qwen9B uses temperature 0.2, six recent exchanges, a 4k context and RAM preloading. The single shared 9B file is now on the C-drive SSD (12.7 GB remains free); the other candidates stay available on D. Your CPU/GPU hardware choices are retained. Change models under Settings > AI; GPU and Max speed remain available. Max speed temporarily limits game rendering while the model works.

blocks.text: 16 turns per model; CUDA/Max speed, temperature 0.2, two recent exchanges to exercise saved recall. Gemma used 2k context; others 4k. Observed menu times exclude initial loading. They are not controlled world-performance benchmarks. Observed D-drive loads varied from 4 to 157 seconds; cache state was not controlled. The selected 9B file has since moved to the SSD. *4B gave the correct player age, but also stated its own age, triggering the strict matcher.

images.caption: Actual spoken replies from Qwen9B in the camp. The questions and full requests are preserved in the verification record.

blocks.text: 60 core checks passed. Two physical camp runs passed 34 functional checks each: interaction, listening, approach, temporary actions, saved-memory restoration and host cleanup. Manual review separately caught Gemma’s wrong age answer. A final 16-turn Qwen regression passed after the recall-question fix. Camp tests used 18 GPU layers, 8 CPU threads, 2 GB VRAM reserve and capped rendering to leave room for video.

Local replies can still invent details: Qwen gave the correct age but incorrectly said the player had told it that age. The current display still waits for a complete validated reply; streamed text and voice are not part of this update.
